items.title: Bobby Hutcherson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: We did a concert the day that Kennedy was assassinated – the next day, at Judson Hall, me, Tony, Grachan, Eddie Kahn.

ctx.x: We’re putting our – we’re going to the Port Authority, putting drums and vibes underneath a bus. We get to the club, and Jackie’s not there. The owner of the club says, “Where’s Jackie?” We said he’ll be here soon. Finally, the door opens up, and Jackie comes through the door with his horn. He walks in. He comes and stands in front of me, and his pants are completely ripped out in the back. We’re – Tony says, “Jackie.” Jackie says, “I know, I know, I know.” “Jackie!” Jackie says, “Wooo, it’s hot up here.”

The next thing is he says, because it’s so early, he says, “Give me a ham and eggs on the rocks,” and we just died laughing. We did a concert the day that Kennedy was assassinated – the next day, at Judson Hall, me, Tony, Grachan, Eddie Kahn. The nation was in mourning. Nobody was – one guy showed up and sat right in the middle of the audience, so he can get stereo sound. So we said – I said, “Jackie, are we going to play?” He said, “Yes, we’re going to play. Every time you play, it’s important. It’s the most…
We’re going to stop. We’ve got to change the tape. Boy, Bobby, you got some stories, man.
